contributions.headingText: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK) is a rare malignant renal tumour of childhood, characterized histologically by variably clear tumour cells and distinctive arborizing fibrovascular septa, and molecularly by BCOR mutations or YWHAE::NUTM2 gene fusion.
8964/3 Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney
2C90.Y & XH0765 Other specified malignant neoplasms of kidney, except renal pelvis & Clear cell sarcoma of kidney
Not recommended: bone-metastasizing renal tumour of childhood.
CCSK arises in the kidney and is often centred in the renal medulla. Bilateral CCSK has not been reported.
The affected child may have nonspecific features of abdominal distension, pain, a palpable abdominal mass, or gross haematuria.
CCSK constitutes 3–5% of malignant renal tumours in childhood, ranking a distant second after nephroblastoma. The M:F ratio is 2:1. The mean age at diagnosis is 3 years {4065884}.
There are no known risk factors. CCSK is a sporadic tumour. There are no reports of familial CCSK.

CCSK is characterized by mutations affecting BCOR (either an in-frame internal tandem duplication [ITD] affecting exon 15 {26098867} or a BCOR::CCNB3 gene fusion {28833375}) or by YWHAE::NUTM2 gene fusion {22294382}. These mutations result in oncogenic upregulation of BCOR, which is a component of non-canonical PRC1.1 {16943429}. The specific mechanism of molecular pathogenesis is currently unknown.
CCSK often manifests as a solitary large renal tumour with its epicentre at the renal medulla. The cut surface is pale tan-grey and fleshy; mucoid to cystic areas may be present.

CCSK has varied histological patterns {10632483}. The classic pattern is most common and is usually present at least focally {10632483; 30628851}. The features include plump ovoid tumour cells demarcated into broad trabeculae or nests by distinctive arborizing fibrovascular septa. Tumour cells have barely perceptible cytoplasm and monomorphic nuclei with dispersed chromatin and indistinct nucleoli. The nuclei and cytoplasm often have a clear appearance, from which this tumour derives its name. The cellular pattern has similar tumour cells that are more closely packed, with frequent nuclear overlapping {10632483}. The myxoid pattern features increased mucopolysaccharide matrix, which may form mucoid pools and cysts {10632483}. The sclerosing pattern features hyalinized collagen, which may resemble osteoid {10632483}. The epithelioid pattern has tumour cells aligned in acini or elongated trabeculae mimicking the epithelial structures that may be seen in nephroblastoma {10632483}. The palisading pattern features nuclear palisading that resembles Verocay bodies of schwannomas {10632483}. The spindled pattern has elongated tumour cells resembling those of spindle cell sarcomas {10632483}. Rare tumours have anaplasia, defined in the same way as for nephroblastomas {10632483}. Posttreatment relapses may resemble myxoma or fibromatosis histologically.

Immunohistochemistry

Immunoreactivity for both cyclin D1 and BCOR in a diffuse nuclear staining pattern provides robust support for the diagnosis of CCSK {28833375; 25751590; 25556515}. However, although sensitive, cyclin D1 is not perfectly specific; and BCOR is neither perfectly sensitive nor specific. Other positive markers include vimentin, p75-NGFR, BCL2, TLE1, and SATB2 {32364435; 28426529}. CCSK is negative for CD34, S100, desmin, cytokeratins, and EMA {8396229}. CCSK with BCOR::CCNB3 gene fusion expresses cyclin B3 {28877060}.

The three characteristic mutations of CCSK are (in decreasing order of frequency) BCOR exon 15 ITD, YWHAE::NUTM2 fusion, and BCOR::CCNB3 fusion. These three sequence alterations are mutually exclusive.

Essential: characteristic histomorphology (ovoid tumour cells with nuclear and/or cytoplasmic clearing at least focally, distinctive arborizing fibrovascular septa, and immunoreactivity for cyclin D1 and BCOR).

Desirable: in cases with atypical histomorphology or immunophenotype: molecular identification of BCOR exon 15 ITD or YWHAE::NUTM2 fusion or BCOR::CCNB3 fusion.
Staging follows the same International Society of Paediatric Oncology (SIOP) or Children’s Oncology Group (COG) staging systems as used for nephroblastomas.

CCSK has 5-year event-free and overall survival rates of 65–85% and 75–90%, respectively, with intensive multiagent chemotherapy and radiation therapy {22579455}. Approximately 16% of patients relapse {24937667}. Relapse may be late {10632483}. CCSK may metastasize to unusual sites such as bone, orbit, and brain. The clinical course is not predicted by histological pattern or mutation findings.
